headline: Google has released Gmail Live, a voice feature that lets paying Google AI subscribers search their inbox by asking questions in conversation.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a real release of a Google feature, limited to paying subscribers, with the exact date of the rollout not stated.
importance_line: Subscribers to Google's AI Plus, Pro and Ultra plans can find details in their email by speaking, which also means an AI reads their inbox, while free users and, for now, business customers do not get it; answer quality has not been independently tested.
summary: Engadget reports that Google's Gmail Live, announced at its I/O developer conference, is out of beta for subscribers to Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra, letting them ask spoken questions such as "What's my flight's gate number?" and get answers drawn from their inbox. Google is also rolling out similar voice features for Keep notes (all three plans) and Docs (Pro and Ultra only), with Google Workspace business customers promised access "coming soon".
notes: Read Engadget in full. Engadget says the features are rolling out 'this week'; the exact start day is not given, so no staleness cut. The quoted example is from Google's announcement as quoted by Engadget.
